898	# ─── _render_pipeline_end <status> [stage] [rc] (#525) ───────────────────────
899	# Emits the terminal banner that closes a pipeline run, framed with ═ (U+2550)
900	# to distinguish the pipeline boundary from the stage divider (━) and stage-io
901	# banners (─). Two-line layout:
902	#
903	#   ════════════════ pipeline.end ════════════════ HH:MM:SS UTC
904	#   <glyph> Pipeline <status_word>: status=<X> run_id=<Y> issue=<N> (took <dur>)
905	#
906	# Frame bars colored BLUE (chrome). Glyph + leading status word inherit the
907	# verdict class color (foreground signal). Right-aligned timestamp via the
908	# same width math as _render_stage_divider — degrades to a symmetric divider
909	# (no timestamp) when mid_bar <= 2.
910	#
911	# Writes to fd 2 so it composes correctly with other operator lines (info /
912	# success / error) under the same output redirection rules. Banner is emitted
913	# AFTER the pipeline.end JSONL event so the durable event is fail-closed
914	# against banner-write failures.
915	_render_pipeline_end() {
916	    local status="${1:-unknown}"
917	    local stage_hint="${2:-}"
918	    local rc_hint="${3:-}"
919	    local run_id="${_runner_run_id:-?}"
920	    local issue="${_runner_issue:-?}"
921	    # Best-effort value gathering. Each `$(...)` here forks a helper that may
922	    # itself fork an external (awk in the duration token, date/tput in the
923	    # clock/width helpers). Most call sites invoke this banner DIRECTLY under the
924	    # runner's `set -e` (e.g. the cycle/stage abort + LLM/scope-abort paths) —
925	    # not wrapped in `|| true` — so a transient under-load fork failure in any
926	    # one of these bare assignments would trip errexit and abort the render
927	    # BEFORE the printf block, silently dropping the operator's terminal banner
928	    # mid-teardown. `|| fallback` neutralizes errexit at each assignment so the
929	    # banner is always emitted once the function is reached, on every call site.
930	    # (#1156)
931	    local dur; dur="$(_runner_pipeline_duration_token)" || dur='?s'
932	    local glyph; glyph="$(_pipeline_status_glyph "$status")" || glyph='✗'
933	    local color; color="$(_pipeline_status_color "$status")" || color=''
934	    local frame="${BLUE:-}"
935	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)" || ts='??:??:?? UTC'
936	    local width; width="$(_term_width)" || width=80
937	
938	    # Map status → operator-friendly verb for line 2. Tracks event payload
939	    # verbatim so "status=<X>" agrees with the verb. ("success" in legacy
940	    # event payloads renders as "complete" — see ADR-015 §v5 amendment).
941	    local word
942	    case "$status" in
943	        success|complete)        word="complete" ;;
944	        complete_unconverged)    word="complete_unconverged" ;;
945	        failed)                  word="failed" ;;
946	        interrupted)             word="interrupted" ;;
947	        aborted)                 word="aborted" ;;
948	        preflight_failed)        word="preflight_failed" ;;
949	        *)                       word="$status" ;;
950	    esac
951	
952	    local label=" pipeline.end "
953	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
954	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
955	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
956	
957	    local detail_status="status=${status}"
958	    [[ -n "$stage_hint" ]] && detail_status+=" stage=${stage_hint}"
959	    [[ -n "$rc_hint"    ]] && detail_status+=" rc=${rc_hint}"
960	
961	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
962	        # Degraded layout — drop timestamp from the header.
963	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
964	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
965	        local bar
966	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
967	        bar="${bar// /═}"
968	        {
969	            printf '\n'
970	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$frame" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$frame" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
971	            printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
972	                "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
973	                "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
974	        } >&2
975	        _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
976	        return 0
977	    fi
978	
979	    local lbar rbar
980	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /═}"
981	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /═}"
982	    {
983	        printf '\n'
984	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
985	            "$frame" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
986	            "$frame" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
987	        printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
988	            "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
989	            "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
990	    } >&2
991	    _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
992	}
993	
994	# _runner_render_open_items <status> — #2330 (ADR-068 §8): a run that did not
995	# pass ends by saying why in words and naming each open item, with what would
996	# settle it. pipeline.end keeps the engine's code; this is what a reader sees.
997	_runner_render_open_items() {
998	    case "${1:-}" in failed|interrupted|aborted) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
999	    [[ -n "${_runner_state_file:-}" ]] && declare -F open_items_markdown >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
1000	    local sd="${_runner_state_file%/*}" items n
1001	    items="$(open_items_markdown "$sd")" || items=""
1002	    n=0; [[ -n "$items" ]] && n="$(grep -c '^[0-9][0-9]*\. ' <<< "$items" || true)"
1003	    {
1004	        printf 'The run %s.\n' "$(run_end_words "${_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON:-}" "$n")"
1005	        [[ -n "$items" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$items"
1006	    } >&2
1007	}
1008	
1009	# ─── _render_stage_divider <stage> (#492, ts: #508) ──────────────────────────
1010	# Emits a blank line + a heavy horizontal rule (━ U+2501) with the stage name
1011	# centered in stage-color, then another blank line — written to fd 2 so it
1012	# survives the same redirection rules as ▸/✓/✗ info lines. Used on every
1013	# stage transition (between eb_emit_event "stage.start" and "▸ Running stage")
1014	# so the operator's eye finds the next stage boundary at a glance.
1015	#
1016	# #508: right-align an HH:MM:SS UTC timestamp on the divider, mirroring the
1017	# stage-io banner header right-alignment (_stage_io_compose_banner). Width
1018	# math (no bookend glyphs in this layout — just bars + label + sep + ts):
1019	#   visible = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (space) + len(ts)
1020	#   left_bar = (width - len(label) - len(ts) - 1) / 2
1021	#   mid_bar  = width - left_bar - len(label) - len(ts) - 1
1022	# Degrade rule: when mid_bar <= 2 (very narrow terminals) we drop the
1023	# timestamp and emit the legacy symmetric divider so layout stays legible.
1024	_render_stage_divider() {
1025	    local stage="$1"
1026	    local width
1027	    width="$(_term_width)"
1028	    local color
1029	    color="$(_stage_color "$stage")"
1030	    local label=" ${stage} "
1031	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)"
1032	
1033	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
1034	    # Visible width = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (sep) + len(ts).
1035	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
1036	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
1037	
1038	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
1039	        # Degraded: legacy symmetric divider, no timestamp (narrow terminal).
1040	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1041	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1042	        local bar
1043	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1044	        bar="${bar// /━}"
1045	        {
1046	            printf '\n'
1047	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$color" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$color" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1048	            printf '\n'
1049	            # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the existing leading
1050	            # \n above, produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages.
1051	            # Cycle sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1052	            printf '\n'
1053	        } >&2
1054	        return 0
1055	    fi
1056	
1057	    local lbar rbar
1058	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /━}"
1059	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /━}"
1060	    {
1061	        printf '\n'
1062	        # %b on colored fragments so \033[...] resolves like echo -e elsewhere.
1063	        # Timestamp is plain text outside color escapes — NO_COLOR keeps it.
1064	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
1065	            "$color" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1066	            "$color" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
1067	        printf '\n'
1068	        # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the leading \n above,
1069	        # produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages. Cycle
1070	        # sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1071	        printf '\n'
1072	    } >&2
1073	}
1074	
1075	# ─── Cycle banner helpers (#524, ADR-015 §v6, ADR-021) ───────────────────────
1076	# Operator-fd-2 chrome for outer cycles (ADR-021). These render a visual
1077	# hierarchy that nests cleanly with the existing stage-transition divider
1078	# (_render_stage_divider) so the operator can see cycle entry, per-iter
1079	# boundaries, per-iter outcomes, and cycle exit in the scrollback.
1080	#
1081	# Glyph + color ladder (heaviest → lightest):
1082	#   ━━━ (U+2501) stage transition   — BOLD BLUE (handled in _render_stage_divider)
1083	#   ═══ (U+2550) cycle entry/exit   — LIGHT_BLUE
1084	#   ─── (U+2500) cycle iter divider — CYAN
1085	#
1086	# Routing contract (silent-failure mitigations):
1087	#   - All 4 helpers write to fd 2 ONLY. Hardcoded `>&2`. NEVER capture in $(…)
1088	#     — output would vanish. Banner emit follows event emit (event=durable,
1089	#     banner=best-effort).
1090	#   - `{ ...; } >&2 2>/dev/null || true` is used so a broken stderr can never
1091	#     abort the cycle. Each block is a single printf wrapped in the redirect
1092	#     group so SIGINT during banner emit cannot race on partial writes.
1093	#   - These banners are fd-2 ONLY and NEVER appear in the PR comment body
1094	#     rendered by gh_comment. Operator chrome only.
1095	#
1096	# Determinism: honors ZBUILD_TERM_WIDTH_OVERRIDE + ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE
1097	# via _term_width / _runner_now_short (same contract as _render_stage_divider).
1098	
1099	# ─── _render_cycle_entry <cycle_id> <max> <stages_csv> ───────────────────────
1100	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering cycle <id>` line + DIM trailer
1101	# (max + stages). Emitted by the runner BEFORE cycle_orchestrator_run so the
1102	# operator's eye finds the cycle boundary before the first iter divider.
1103	_render_cycle_entry() {
1104	    local cycle_id="$1" max="$2" stages_csv="${3:-}" description="${4:-}"
1105	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1106	    local label=" cycle: ${cycle_id} "
1107	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1108	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1109	    local bar
1110	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1111	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1112	    {
1113	        printf '\n'
1114	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1115	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1116	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1117	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering cycle: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1118	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1119	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$cycle_id" "${RESET:-}"
1120	        # #831: operator-facing description on its own DIM line, between the
1121	        # Entering-cycle headline and the (max_iterations=…) trailer. Skipped
1122	        # entirely when description is empty so templates without it render
1123	        # identically to the pre-#831 banner (golden tests stay valid).
1124	        if [[ -n "$description" ]]; then
1125	            printf '%b  %s%b\n' "${DIM:-}" "$description" "${RESET:-}"
1126	        fi
1127	        printf '%b  (max_iterations=%s · stages=%s)%b\n' \
1128	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$stages_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1129	        printf '\n'
1130	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1131	}
1132	
1133	# ─── _render_parallel_entry <group_id> <max_parallel> <members_csv> ──────────
1134	# ADR-039 (#1131): clone of _render_cycle_entry for a parallel stage group.
1135	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering parallel group <id>` line + DIM
1136	# trailer (max_parallel + members). Emitted by the runner BEFORE
1137	# parallel_group_run so the operator's eye finds the group boundary first.
1138	_render_parallel_entry() {
1139	    local group_id="$1" max="$2" members_csv="${3:-}"
1140	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1141	    local label=" parallel: ${group_id} "
1142	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1143	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1144	    local bar
1145	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1146	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1147	    {
1148	        printf '\n'
1149	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1150	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1151	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1152	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering parallel group: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1153	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1154	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$group_id" "${RESET:-}"
1155	        printf '%b  (max_parallel=%s · members=%s)%b\n' \
1156	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$members_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1157	        printf '\n'
1158	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1159	}
1160	
1161	# ─── _render_parallel_group_complete <group_id> <member_count> <failure_count> ─
1162	# Issue OUT (ADR-039): DIM trailer after a parallel group's per-member lines,
1163	# mirroring _render_cycle_exit's role for cycles. e.g.
1164	# `▸ review_lenses complete — 5 members, 0 blocking`.
1165	_render_parallel_group_complete() {
1166	    local group_id="$1" count="${2:-0}" fail="${3:-0}"
1167	    {
1168	        printf '%b▸ %s complete — %s members, %s blocking%b\n' \
1169	            "${DIM:-}" "$group_id" "$count" "$fail" "${RESET:-}"
1170	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1171	}
1172	
1173	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_divider <cycle_id> <iter> <max> ───────────────────────
1174	# Light `─` CYAN sub-divider for each iter boundary, e.g.
1175	# `─── build_test_cycle iter 2/5 ─────`. When this cycle is nested inside
1176	# another cycle the orchestrator has already set ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX (e.g.
1177	# `4.1`) — surface it as a `[<prefix>]` prefix so operators can tell at a
1178	# glance which outer iter this divider belongs to:
1179	#   outer (no prefix): `─── build_review_cycle iter 1/2 ───`
1180	#   inner (prefix set): `─── [4.1] build_test_cycle iter 1/3 ───`
1181	# Reuses the seq-prefix machinery from Wave 19-B #718 / cycle-orchestrator.sh:888
1182	# — no new plumbing, no hook-signature change. Emitted by the orchestrator's
1183	# iter-begin hook BEFORE the first per-stage banner of the iter.
1184	_render_cycle_iter_divider() {
1185	    local cycle_id="$1" iter="$2" max="$3"
1186	    local prefix="${ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX:-}"
1187	    local label
1188	    if [[ -n "$prefix" ]]; then
1189	        label=" [${prefix}] ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1190	    else
1191	        label=" ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1192	    fi
1193	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1194	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1195	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1196	    local bar
1197	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1198	    bar="${bar// /─}"
1199	    {
1200	        printf '\n%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1201	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1202	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1203	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1204	}
1205	
1206	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_complete <iter> <verdict> <score> <fc> <elapsed_s> ──
1207	# Per-iter DIM trailer line e.g. `↳ iter 2 complete: verdict=pass score=-1
1208	# failure_count=1 elapsed=4s`. Emitted by the orchestrator's iter-complete
1209	# hook AFTER the `cycle.iteration.complete` event is durable. #1254: the
1210	# `score` axis (progress − defects) replaced the retired `velocity` label so
1211	# the per-iter line matches the OUTPUT banner's health score.
1212	_render_cycle_iter_complete() {
1213	    local iter="$1" verdict="$2" score="$3" failure_count="$4" elapsed_s="$5"
1214	    {
1215	        printf '%b↳ iter %s complete: verdict=%s score=%s failure_count=%s elapsed=%ss%b\n' \
1216	            "${DIM:-}" "$iter" "$verdict" "$score" "$failure_count" "$elapsed_s" "${RESET:-}"
1217	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1218	}
1219	
1220	# ─── _render_cycle_exit <cycle_id> <reason> <iter> <max> ──────────────────────
1221	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + verdict-glyph line mapping termination reason
1222	# to glyph + color (see #524 spec).
1223	#   converged       → ✓ GREEN+BOLD
1224	#   max_iterations  → ✗ RED+BOLD
1225	#   plateau         → ✗ RED+BOLD
1226	#   divergence      → ✗ RED+BOLD
1227	#   aborted         → ⚠ YELLOW+BOLD

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/orch/local_engine.sh — shared dispatch/collect/poll/shutdown for the
3	# local-execution orchestrator backends (orch-bash-parallel, orch-ruflo-hive).
4	# Extracted from those two plugins in #281 because they had ~80% duplication
5	# and the #269 normaliser fix had to be applied twice (and still missed
6	# orch-mock — caught belatedly in #278). Single source of truth now.
7	#
8	# Pool layout (caller chooses prefix + pid subdir name):
9	#   <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/<slot>.pid       — wrapper subshell PID
10	#   <pool_dir>/results/<slot>.{stdout,stderr,exit,inner_pid}
11	#
12	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; no set -euo pipefail.
13	
14	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ENGINE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
15	_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ENGINE_LOADED=1
16	
17	_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
18	_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT="$(cd "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
19	
20	# Defensive source: warn (scripts/lib/helpers.sh).
21	if ! declare -F warn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
22	    source "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
23	fi
24	
25	# Load process-group kill helpers (zbuild_pg_kill, zbuild_pid_kill).
26	if ! declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
27	    source "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
28	fi
29	
30	# _orch_local_make_slot_id — collision-resistant slot id (epoch-ns + PID + rand)
31	_orch_local_make_slot_id() {
32	    date +%s%N
33	    printf -- '-%s-' "$$"
34	    openssl rand -hex 8 2>/dev/null || printf '%05d%05d%05d' $RANDOM $RANDOM $RANDOM
35	}
36	
37	
38	# _orch_local_dispatch_workunit <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <work_unit> <caller_tag>
39	# Dispatches <work_unit> (must be an executable file path) in a background
40	# subshell. Records wrapper PID and inner PID; installs trap to propagate
41	# SIGTERM/EXIT to the inner process.
42	#
43	# Output: prints slot_id to stdout AND sets the global _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID.
44	# Callers needing the slot_id after dispatch (e.g. for downstream telemetry)
45	# MUST read the global, NOT use command substitution: `$(_orch_local_dispatch_workunit ...)`
46	# forks a subshell whose EXIT trap (installed by test-helpers.sh or similar)
47	# `pkill -P $$`s the wrapper subshell we just spawned. The global pattern
48	# avoids that subshell entirely. (Caught in #282 second-round review.)
49	#
50	# Returns 0 on successful dispatch, 1 on validation/permission failure.
51	_orch_local_dispatch_workunit() {
52	    local pool_dir="$1"
53	    local pid_subdir="$2"
54	    local work_unit="$3"
55	    local caller_tag="${4:-orch_local}"
56	
57	    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID=""
58	
59	    if [[ ! -f "$work_unit" || ! -x "$work_unit" ]]; then
60	        warn "${caller_tag}: work_unit must be a path to an executable file: ${work_unit}" || true
61	        return 1
62	    fi
63	
64	    # Ensure pool dirs exist even if the caller skipped pre-spawn.
65	    mkdir -p "${pool_dir}/results" "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" 2>/dev/null || {
66	        warn "${caller_tag}: pool dir is not writable: ${pool_dir}" || true
67	        return 1
68	    }
69	
70	    local slot_id
71	    slot_id="$(_orch_local_make_slot_id | tr -d '\n')"
72	    local result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"
73	
74	    # Background subshell: writes inner work-unit PID, traps on exit to
75	    # propagate signals, then waits for inner and writes .exit file.
76	    (
77	        local rc=0 inner=0
78	        # #2108: dispatched from a `<<< "$roles_out"` loop — never its stdin.
79	        bash "$work_unit" </dev/null > "${result_base}.stdout" 2> "${result_base}.stderr" &
80	        inner=$!
81	        echo "$inner" > "${result_base}.inner_pid"
82	        trap 'kill -KILL "$inner" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT INT TERM
83	        wait "$inner" || rc=$?
84	        trap - EXIT INT TERM
85	        echo "$rc" > "${result_base}.exit"
86	    ) &
87	    local worker_pid=$!
88	    echo "$worker_pid" > "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/${slot_id}.pid"
89	    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID="$slot_id"
90	    echo "$slot_id"
91	    return 0
92	}
93	
94	# _orch_local_collect_results <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <timeout_s>
95	# Polls .exit files for every slot in <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/; streams
96	# stdout/stderr. Returns the normalised orch contract code:
97	#   0 = all dispatched work units exited 0  (pool dir removed)
98	#   1 = otherwise (pool dir preserved); _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME says which —
99	#       `failed` (all exited non-zero) or `partial` (at least one passed).
100	#       #1850 (ADR-054 §4): `partial` used to be rc 2.
101	# Work-unit exit codes are normalised — original rc is not passed through.
102	# Single source of truth for the normaliser (#269 + #278 + #281).
103	_orch_local_collect_results() {
104	    local pool_dir="$1"
105	    local pid_subdir="$2"
106	    local timeout_s="${3:-0}"
107	    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
108	
109	    [[ -d "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" ]] || { _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"; return 0; }
110	
111	    local pass_count=0 fail_count=0
112	    local deadline=0
113	    [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 ]] && deadline=$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)} + timeout_s ))
114	
115	    local pid_file slot_id result_base wrapper_pid inner_pid rc
116	    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
117	        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
118	        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
119	        result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"
120	        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
121	        inner_pid=""
122	        [[ -f "${result_base}.inner_pid" ]] && inner_pid="$(cat "${result_base}.inner_pid")"
123	
124	        while [[ ! -f "${result_base}.exit" ]]; do
125	            if [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 && "${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)}" -ge "$deadline" ]]; then
126	                if declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
127	                    zbuild_pg_kill "$wrapper_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
128	                    [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && zbuild_pid_kill "$inner_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
129	                else
130	                    kill -TERM "$wrapper_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
131	                    [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && kill -TERM "$inner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
132	                fi
133	                echo "124" > "${result_base}.exit"
134	                break
135	            fi
136	            sleep 0.1  # fork-budget-exempt: polls until the slot exits — the count is how long it ran (#2236)
137	        done
138	
139	        rc="$(cat "${result_base}.exit" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)"
140	        [[ -f "${result_base}.stdout" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stdout"
141	        [[ -f "${result_base}.stderr" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stderr" >&2
142	        if [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
143	            pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
144	        else
145	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
146	        fi
147	    done
148	
149	    if [[ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
150	        rm -rf "$pool_dir"
151	        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
152	        return 0
153	    elif [[ "$pass_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
154	        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="partial"
155	        return 1
156	    else
157	        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
158	        return 1
159	    fi
160	}
161	
162	# _orch_local_shutdown_pool <pool_dir> <pid_subdir>
163	# Best-effort SIGTERM → 0.5s → SIGKILL on every slot, then rm -rf the pool dir.
164	# Idempotent — safe to call on non-existent pools.
165	_orch_local_shutdown_pool() {
166	    local pool_dir="$1"
167	    local pid_subdir="$2"
168	
169	    [[ -d "$pool_dir" ]] || return 0
170	
171	    local pid_file slot_id wrapper_pid inner_pid
172	    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
173	        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
174	        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
175	        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
176	        inner_pid=""
177	        [[ -f "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid" ]] && \
178	            inner_pid="$(cat "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid")"
179	        if declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
180	            zbuild_pg_kill "$wrapper_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
181	            [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && zbuild_pid_kill "$inner_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
182	        else
183	            kill -TERM "$wrapper_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
184	            [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && kill -TERM "$inner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
185	        fi
186	    done
187	    rm -rf "$pool_dir"
188	    return 0
189	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scripts/lib/proc-group.sh — process-group resolution and kill helpers.
3	# Extracted from core/router/route.sh (Wave 15-G, #687) so the test stage and
4	# any other long-running spawn share one implementation (#1748).
5	# Sourced library: no set -euo pipefail.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED=1
9	
10	# #2056: there is no setsid prefix any more. Process groups come from `set -m`
11	# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
12	# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
13	#
14	# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
15	# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
16	# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
17	# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
18	# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
19	# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
20	# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
21	#
22	# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
23	# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.
24	
25	# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
26	# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
27	# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
28	zbuild_pg_resolve() {
29	    local _pid="${1:-}"
30	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
31	    local _child _self
32	    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
33	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
34	    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
35	        printf '%s' "$_child"
36	        return 0
37	    fi
38	    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
39	    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
40	    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
41	    #
42	    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
43	    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
44	    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
45	    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
46	    # about.
47	    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
48	        printf '%s' "$_pid"
49	    fi
50	}
51	
52	# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group
53	# and single-PID paths so both get the same grace — the escalation is the whole
54	# contract, and a caller that skips it is indistinguishable from a plain KILL.
55	#
56	# Synchronous by construction (#905): the `{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL; } &` backstop
57	# this replaces could outlive the caller that armed it, so teardown returned
58	# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
59	# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
60	# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
61	_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
62	    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
63	    # as an option.
64	    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
65	    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
66	    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
67	    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
68	        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
69	        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
70	        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
71	    done
72	    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
73	}
74	
75	# A non-numeric grace would evaluate to 0 in the arithmetic context above, so the
76	# poll loop would never run and the target would go straight to KILL — silently
77	# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
78	_zbuild_pg_grace() {
79	    local _g="${1:-1}"
80	    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
81	}
82	
83	# zbuild_pg_record_pgid <file> — the pgid out of a `.pgid` record.
84	#
85	# ONE reader, because there are two formats on disk and three places that read
86	# them (#2018). The engine's dispatch record is `<pgid>\t<leader start time>`;
87	# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
88	# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
89	# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
90	# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
91	# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.
92	#
93	# Prints nothing and returns 1 when there is no usable pgid, so a caller can
94	# still distinguish "no record" from "record says 1234".
95	zbuild_pg_record_pgid() {
96	    local _f="${1:-}" _pgid=""
97	    [[ -n "$_f" && -f "$_f" ]] || return 1
98	    IFS=$'\t' read -r _pgid _ 2>/dev/null < "$_f" || true
99	    [[ "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
100	    printf '%s' "$_pgid"
101	}
102	
103	# zbuild_pg_register <pgid> — record a process group the caller just created.
104	#
105	# ADR-062 §1 had the ENGINE record this at dispatch. It could not, and the reason
106	# is structural: a stage is a bash function call, not a subprocess, so at the
107	# dispatch seam no group exists yet. That code fell back to `$$`'s group — the
108	# engine's own — which teardown then skipped, correctly, because signalling your
109	# own group takes the runner down with it. Every record was unkillable, every
110	# record was skipped, and §2's kill loop never freed anything (#2024).
111	#
112	# So the direction reverses: whoever CREATES a group registers it. Two sites do,
113	# and only two — `tool/test`'s `set -m` suite and the router's `setsid` spawn.
114	#
115	# Refusing to register our own group is the invariant, not a safety check. A
116	# record naming the registrar's own group is strictly worse than no record: it
117	# cannot be acted on, and it makes the mechanism look live while it does nothing
118	# — which is exactly how the original defect survived #2001, #2018 and an ADR.
119	#
120	# Fail-open throughout: a spawn is never refused because bookkeeping was
121	# unavailable. Silence here costs a possible leak; failing here costs the run.
122	zbuild_pg_register() {
123	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
124	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
125	    local _self
126	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
127	    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
128	    local _sd="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
129	    [[ -n "$_sd" && -d "$_sd" ]] || return 0
130	    local _stage="${2:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
131	    [[ -n "$_stage" ]] || return 0
132	    # One path component, sanitised the same way stage scratch keys are, so no
133	    # stage name can climb out of runtime/.
134	    _stage="${_stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
135	    local _dir="${_sd}/runtime/stages"
136	    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
137	    # #2018 format: the leader's start time proves the pgid still names what
138	    # recorded it, so a later sweep cannot signal a recycled pid.
139	    local _start
140	    _start="$(ps -o lstart= -p "$_pgid" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' || true)"
141	    printf '%s\t%s' "$_pgid" "$_start" > "${_dir}/${_stage}.pgid" 2>/dev/null || true
142	    return 0
143	}
144	
145	# TERM then KILL a whole process group. `-PGID` is the negative-pid convention.
146	zbuild_pg_kill() {
147	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
148	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
149	    # Refuse our own group: `kill -- -PGID` from inside it takes down the runner.
150	    local _self
151	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
152	    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
153	    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "-$_pgid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
154	}
155	
156	# TERM then KILL a single PID — the path taken when no group could be proven.
157	# It gets the same grace as the group path: a suite that flushes coverage or
158	# writes partial results on SIGTERM needs the window wherever it is killed from.
159	zbuild_pid_kill() {
160	    local _pid="${1:-}"
161	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
162	    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "$_pid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
163	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/pipeline/template.sh — Template loading and stage resolution (issue #208)
3	# ADR-009 (platform-aware modularity), ADR-013 (canonical stage sequence)
4	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
5	
6	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_TEMPLATE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
7	_ZBUILD_TEMPLATE_LOADED=1
8	
9	_ZBUILD_TEMPLATE_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
10	_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "$_ZBUILD_TEMPLATE_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
11	
12	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
13	source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
14	# shellcheck source=../plugin-registry/registry.sh
15	source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/registry.sh"
16	# ADR-027 (Wave 17-B #703): template.deprecated_shape event on old-shape load.
17	# Defensive source — event-bus is a no-op when ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL is unset.
18	if ! declare -F eb_emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
19	    # shellcheck source=../event-bus/event-bus.sh
20	    source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
21	fi
22	
23	# ADR-047 §5 (#1299): stage membership + order are NOT an engine-owned hardcoded
24	# roster. Membership is enforced by the manifest-derived resolvability preflight
25	# (_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability, runner.sh — every leaf must resolve to a
26	# plugin) and order by the upstream-input data-dependency DAG (contract-validator.sh).
27	# The retired _ZBUILD_CANONICAL_STAGES array + ZBUILD_LEGACY_STAGE_VALIDATION
28	# kill-switch (the strangler escape hatch) are deleted; the preflight + DAG are the
29	# sole enforcement.
30	
31	# Module-level state — populated by load_template
32	_TPL_DEFAULT_STRATEGY="fanout"
33	_TPL_MERGE_POLICY="auto_unless_flagged"
34	_TPL_STAGES=()
35	# #1831: ordered stage ids that run on EVERY exit path (success, non-zero rc,
36	# SIGINT, SIGTERM, timeout). Declared by the template's top-level `always_run:`
37	# list, NOT part of _TPL_STAGES[] — an always-run stage is not in the flow.
38	_TPL_ALWAYS_RUN=()
39	# ADR-021 (#512): list of dispatch units in template order. Each entry is
40	# "stage:<id>" or "cycle:<id>". Empty `cycles:` block → every unit is "stage:<id>"
41	# (backwards-compat — runner behavior identical to today).
42	_TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS=()
43	# ADR-021: list of cycle ids declared in template (in declaration order).
44	_TPL_CYCLES=()
45	# ADR-039 (#1130): list of parallel group ids declared in template (in
46	# declaration order). Sibling of _TPL_CYCLES — a `type: parallel` group folds
47	# to one "parallel:<gid>" dispatch unit. Template-layer parse/validate only;
48	# execution lands in a later issue.
49	_TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS=()
50	# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): list of map group ids declared in template (in
51	# declaration order). A `type: map` group folds to one "map:<gid>" dispatch unit.
52	_TPL_MAP_GROUPS=()
53	
54	# ADR-015 v1 (#438): recognized io.destination tokens. Unknown tokens fail at
55	# template load time with an actionable error listing the valid set.
56	readonly _ZBUILD_IO_DESTINATIONS_VALID=(file stdout gh_comment)
57	
58	load_template() {
59	    local template_file="$1"
60	    if [[ ! -f "$template_file" ]]; then
61	        error "load_template: file not found: $template_file"
62	        return 1
63	    fi
64	    # ADR-036 #1188: remember the source path so lightweight per-stage getters
65	    # (e.g. template_stage_negctl_timeout) can read additive scalar knobs without
66	    # threading them through the pipe-delimited row shape.
67	    _TPL_SOURCE_FILE="$template_file"; export _TPL_SOURCE_FILE
68	
69	    # ADR-021 v2 (#585): legacy top-level `cycles:` block is a hard-break.
70	    # Detect and refuse with a pointer to the migration helper.
71	    if awk 'BEGIN{rc=1} /^cycles:[[:space:]]*$/ {rc=0; exit} END{exit rc}' "$template_file"; then
72	        error "load_template: legacy 'cycles:' block detected in $template_file"
73	        error "  v2 template syntax inlines cycles as stage entries (type: cycle)"
74	        error "  with per-stage attributes hoisted into a top-level"
75	        error "  'stage_definitions:' map (see ADR-021 v2 / issue #585)."
76	        error "  Run: scripts/migrate-template-v2.sh '$template_file' --in-place"
77	        return 1
78	    fi
79	    # ADR-055 §4 (amended 2026-10-12): cycle `feedback:` wires are retired —
80	    # every stage gets every stage's latest output under Previous work
81	    # (ADR-068 §8), so a wire would promise a delivery nothing makes.
82	    if awk 'BEGIN{rc=1} /^[[:space:]]+feedback:([[:space:]]|$)/ {rc=0; exit} END{exit rc}' "$template_file"; then
83	        error "load_template: 'feedback:' is retired (ADR-055 §4) in $template_file"
84	        error "  every stage already gets every stage's latest output under Previous work"
85	        error "  (ADR-068 §8); remove the feedback: block from the cycle."
86	        return 1
87	    fi
88	
89	    _TPL_DEFAULT_STRATEGY="$(yaml_get "$template_file" "defaults.strategy")"
90	    [[ -z "$_TPL_DEFAULT_STRATEGY" ]] && _TPL_DEFAULT_STRATEGY="fanout"
91	
92	    local _raw_merge_policy
93	    _raw_merge_policy="$(yaml_get "$template_file" "merge_policy")"
94	    if [[ -z "$_raw_merge_policy" ]]; then
95	        _TPL_MERGE_POLICY="auto_unless_flagged"
96	    elif [[ "$_raw_merge_policy" == "auto_unless_flagged" || "$_raw_merge_policy" == "auto" || "$_raw_merge_policy" == "manual" ]]; then
97	        _TPL_MERGE_POLICY="$_raw_merge_policy"
98	    else
99	        error "load_template: invalid merge_policy '${_raw_merge_policy}' (valid: auto_unless_flagged | auto | manual)"
100	        return 1
101	    fi
102	    export _TPL_MERGE_POLICY
103	
104	    local _raw_pr_draft
105	    _raw_pr_draft="$(yaml_get "$template_file" "pr_draft")"
106	    if [[ -z "$_raw_pr_draft" ]]; then
107	        _TPL_PR_DRAFT="false"
108	    elif [[ "$_raw_pr_draft" == "true" || "$_raw_pr_draft" == "false" ]]; then
109	        _TPL_PR_DRAFT="$_raw_pr_draft"
110	    else
111	        error "load_template: invalid pr_draft '${_raw_pr_draft}' (valid: true | false)"
112	        return 1
113	    fi
114	    export _TPL_PR_DRAFT
115	
116	    # Scrub ALL _TPL_STAGE_BLOCKING_<id> exports at load-entry, unconditionally.
117	    # BL| rows are emitted only for stages that declare blocking:, so any stale export —
118	    # left by a prior load_template call, by a stage that is absent from this
119	    # template's flow entirely, OR inherited from the process environment on a
120	    # cold-start first load — would otherwise survive and mis-mark a non-blocking
121	    # stage as blocking (ADR-013, issue #952 follow-up to #863). Iterating over
122	    # the prior _TPL_STAGES was a no-op on the first load; prefix expansion over
123	    # the live environment closes that cold-start gap.
124	    local _stale_bl
125	    for _stale_bl in "${!_TPL_STAGE_BLOCKING_@}"; do
126	        # Defensive: only unset well-formed identifier names ([A-Za-z0-9_]+),
127	        # never a name assembled from unvalidated input.
128	        [[ "$_stale_bl" =~ ^_TPL_STAGE_BLOCKING_[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ ]] || continue
129	        unset "$_stale_bl"
130	    done
131	
132	    local _stale_to
133	    for _stale_to in "${!_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_@}"; do
134	        [[ "$_stale_to" =~ ^_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ ]] || continue
135	        unset "$_stale_to"
136	    done
137	
138	    _TPL_STAGES=()
139	    _TPL_ALWAYS_RUN=()
140	    _TPL_CYCLES=()
141	    _TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS=()
142	    _TPL_MAP_GROUPS=()
143	    # ADR-027 (Wave 17-B #703): shape detector. The new shape uses `flow:` at
144	    # top level + per-stage top-level sections discriminated by `type:`. The
145	    # old shape (Wave 15-D era) uses `stages:` + `stage_definitions:`. Detect
146	    # which we're loading; old shape routes through the legacy parsers
147	    # unchanged AND fires `template.deprecated_shape` so operators can find
148	    # stragglers before the shim removal (one release window).
149	    local _tpl_shape="old"
150	    if _tpl_is_new_shape "$template_file"; then
151	        _tpl_shape="new"
152	    else
153	        # Emit the deprecation event with run_id cleared so it does not enter
154	        # any C6-style "last-event-for-this-run" precondition chain (template
155	        # load is a process-level concern, not a pipeline-run event). The
156	        # event still appears in events.jsonl for ops-dashboard visibility.
157	        (
158	            unset ZBUILD_RUN_ID
159	            eb_emit_event "template.deprecated_shape" \
160	                "template_file=$template_file" "shape=pre_adr_027" \
161	                2>/dev/null || true
162	        )
163	    fi
164	
165	    # ADR-021 v2 parser: scan `stages:` block, emitting interleaved S|/IC|
166	    # rows. Inline cycle entries (IC|) reference cycle member stages by id;
167	    # per-stage attrs for those members come from `stage_definitions:` (parsed
168	    # separately below).
169	    # ADR-027 (Wave 17-B): new-shape templates are translated by
170	    # _tpl_translate_new_shape into the same pipe-delimited row format the
171	    # legacy pipeline downstream code already consumes — single internal
172	    # representation; the shim is purely upstream.
173	    local stage_rows defs_rows
174	    if [[ "$_tpl_shape" == "new" ]]; then
175	        local _translated; _translated="$(_tpl_translate_new_shape "$template_file")" || return 1
176	        stage_rows="${_translated%%$'\037'*}"
177	        defs_rows="${_translated#*$'\037'}"
178	    else
179	        stage_rows="$(_tpl_parse_stages_v2 "$template_file")"
180	        defs_rows="$(_tpl_parse_stage_definitions "$template_file")"
181	    fi
182	
183	    # Build map: stage id → "S|<id>|<roles>|<strategy>|<io...>|<router...>"
184	    # First load defs into the map; then non-cycle stage rows from `stages:`
185	    # also feed the map (regular stages declare their own attrs inline).
186	    local -A stage_def_row=()
187	    local row sid rest
188	    while IFS= read -r row; do
189	        [[ -z "$row" ]] && continue
190	        sid="${row%%|*}"
191	        rest="${row#*|}"
192	        stage_def_row["$sid"]="$rest"
193	    done <<< "$defs_rows"
194	
195	    # Phase 1: collect ids in execution order + extract cycle metadata.
196	    local -a collected_ids=()
197	    local -a collected_io_dests=()
198	    local -a collected_io_tail=()
199	    local -a collected_io_redact=()
200	    local -a collected_router_timeout=()
201	    local -a collected_router_max_turns=()
202	    local -a collected_router_max_iterations=()
203	    local -a collected_router_retries=()
204	    local -a stage_data_rows=()
205	
206	    while IFS= read -r row; do
207	        [[ -z "$row" ]] && continue
208	        local tag="${row%%|*}"
209	        local payload="${row#*|}"
210	        case "$tag" in
211	            S)
212	                # Inline regular stage row from `stages:` — full attr payload.
213	                # Format: <id>|<roles>|<strategy>|<io_dests>|<io_tail>|<io_redact>|<rt>|<rmt>|<rmi>|<rretries>
214	                local s_id s_roles s_strat s_iod s_iot s_ior s_rt s_rmt s_rmi s_rre
215	                IFS='|' read -r s_id s_roles s_strat s_iod s_iot s_ior s_rt s_rmt s_rmi s_rre <<< "$payload"
216	                [[ -z "$s_id" ]] && continue
217	                # Also drop into defs map so cycle members can declare attrs
218	                # inline if templates choose to (forward-compat).
219	                stage_def_row["$s_id"]="$s_roles|$s_strat|$s_iod|$s_iot|$s_ior|$s_rt|$s_rmt|$s_rmi|$s_rre"
220	                collected_ids+=("$s_id")
221	                collected_io_dests+=("$s_iod")
222	                collected_io_tail+=("$s_iot")
223	                collected_io_redact+=("$s_ior")
224	                collected_router_timeout+=("$s_rt")
225	                collected_router_max_turns+=("$s_rmt")
226	                collected_router_max_iterations+=("$s_rmi")

933	        tl = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+tail_lines:[[:space:]]*/, "", tl); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", tl); current_io_tail = tl; in_io_dests = 0; next
934	    }
935	    in_stages && entry_kind == "stage" && in_io_block && /^[[:space:]]+redact:/ {
936	        rd = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+redact:[[:space:]]*/, "", rd); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", rd); current_io_redact = rd; in_io_dests = 0; next
937	    }
938	    END { flush_entry() }
939	    ' "$file"
940	}
941	
942	# ─── _tpl_parse_stage_definitions — parse `stage_definitions:` map (v2) ─────
943	# Emits one S|<id>|<roles>|<strategy>|<io_dests>|<io_tail>|<io_redact>|<rt>|<rmt>|<rmi>
944	# row per definition. Same payload shape as _tpl_parse_stage_data so the load
945	# pipeline can consume both streams uniformly.
946	_tpl_parse_stage_definitions() {
947	    local file="$1"
948	    awk '
949	    function trim(s) { sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", s); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", s); return s }
950	    function flush_def() {
951	        if (cur_id == "")
952	            return
953	        print cur_id "|" cur_roles "|" cur_strategy "|" cur_io_dests "|" cur_io_tail "|" cur_io_redact "|" cur_rt "|" cur_rmt "|" cur_rmi "|" cur_rre
954	    }
955	    function reset_def() {
956	        cur_id = ""; cur_roles = ""; cur_strategy = ""
957	        cur_io_dests = ""; cur_io_tail = ""; cur_io_redact = ""
958	        cur_rt = ""; cur_rmt = ""; cur_rmi = ""; cur_rre = ""
959	        in_roles = 0; in_io_block = 0; in_io_dests = 0; in_router_block = 0
960	    }
961	    BEGIN { reset_def() }
962	    /^stage_definitions:[[:space:]]*$/ { in_defs = 1; next }
963	    in_defs && /^[a-zA-Z_]/ { flush_def(); reset_def(); in_defs = 0; next }
964	    # Each top-level def is "  <id>:" (2-space indent).
965	    in_defs && /^[[:space:]]+[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*$/ {
966	        # Distinguish "  <id>:" (indent 2) from deeper "    <field>:" (indent 4+).
967	        line = $0
968	        indent = match(line, /[^ ]/) - 1
969	        if (indent == 2) {
970	            flush_def(); reset_def()
971	            cur_id = line; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", cur_id); gsub(/:[[:space:]]*$/, "", cur_id)
972	            next
973	        }
974	    }
975	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && in_roles && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
976	        item = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", item); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", item)
977	        if (item != "") {
978	            if (cur_roles == "") cur_roles = item
979	            else cur_roles = cur_roles "," item
980	        }
981	        next
982	    }
983	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && in_roles { in_roles = 0 }
984	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && in_io_dests && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
985	        item = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", item); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", item)
986	        if (item != "") {
987	            if (cur_io_dests == "") cur_io_dests = item
988	            else cur_io_dests = cur_io_dests "," item
989	        }
990	        next
991	    }
992	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && in_io_dests { in_io_dests = 0 }
993	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && /^[[:space:]]+roles:/ {
994	        roles_line = $0
995	        if (roles_line ~ /\[/) {
996	            sub(/^[^[]*\[/, "", roles_line)
997	            sub(/\].*$/, "", roles_line)
998	            gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", roles_line)
999	            cur_roles = roles_line
1000	        } else { in_roles = 1 }
1001	        next
1002	    }
1003	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && /^[[:space:]]+strategy:/ {
1004	        in_io_block = 0; in_io_dests = 0; in_router_block = 0
1005	        cur_strategy = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+strategy:[[:space:]]*/, "", cur_strategy); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", cur_strategy)
1006	        next
1007	    }
1008	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && /^[[:space:]]+io:[[:space:]]*$/ { in_io_block = 1; in_router_block = 0; next }
1009	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && /^[[:space:]]+router:[[:space:]]*$/ { in_io_block = 0; in_io_dests = 0; in_router_block = 1; next }
1010	    in_defs && in_router_block && /^[[:space:]]+timeout_s:/ {
1011	        v = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); cur_rt = v; next
1012	    }
1013	    in_defs && in_router_block && /^[[:space:]]+max_turns:/ {
1014	        v = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+max_turns:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); cur_rmt = v; next
1015	    }
1016	    in_defs && in_router_block && /^[[:space:]]+max_iterations:/ {
1017	        v = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+max_iterations:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); cur_rmi = v; next
1018	    }
1019	    in_defs && in_router_block && /^[[:space:]]+retries:/ {
1020	        v = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+retries:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); cur_rre = v; next
1021	    }
1022	    in_defs && in_router_block && /^[[:space:]]+[a-z_]+:/ { next }
1023	    in_defs && in_io_block && /^[[:space:]]+destinations:/ {
1024	        dest_line = $0
1025	        if (dest_line ~ /\[/) {
1026	            sub(/^[^[]*\[/, "", dest_line)
1027	            sub(/\].*$/, "", dest_line)
1028	            gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", dest_line)
1029	            cur_io_dests = dest_line
1030	            in_io_dests = 0
1031	        } else { in_io_dests = 1 }
1032	        next
1033	    }
1034	    in_defs && in_io_block && /^[[:space:]]+tail_lines:/ {
1035	        v = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+tail_lines:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); cur_io_tail = v; in_io_dests = 0; next
1036	    }
1037	    in_defs && in_io_block && /^[[:space:]]+redact:/ {
1038	        v = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+redact:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); cur_io_redact = v; in_io_dests = 0; next
1039	    }
1040	    END { flush_def() }
1041	    ' "$file"
1042	}
1043	
1044	# ─── _tpl_validate_cycles — enforce ADR-021 invariants ───────────────────────
1045	# - stages[] is contiguous subsequence of canonical (_TPL_STAGES) order
1046	# - max_iterations integer 1..10 (REQUIRED)
1047	# - until.stage MUST be in cycle.stages
1048	# - cycles MUST NOT overlap each other
1049	_tpl_validate_cycles() {
1050	    [[ ${#_TPL_CYCLES[@]} -eq 0 ]] && return 0
1051	    local cid prev_end=-1
1052	    local -A seen_stage=()
1053	    for cid in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do
1054	        local safe="${cid//-/_}"
1055	        local stages_var="_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_${safe}"
1056	        local stages_csv="${!stages_var:-}"
1057	        if [[ -z "$stages_csv" ]]; then
1058	            error "cycle '$cid': no stages declared"
1059	            return 1
1060	        fi
1061	        local IFS_save="$IFS"; IFS=','
1062	        # shellcheck disable=SC2206
1063	        local -a cs=($stages_csv)
1064	        IFS="$IFS_save"
1065	
1066	        # Every stage of the loop — its inner loops and parallel groups expanded
1067	        # where they sit (#2271: an outer loop's own stages may sit between its
1068	        # inner loops) — must be a known _TPL_STAGES entry, contiguous and in
1069	        # order. A stage belongs DIRECTLY to at most one loop.
1070	        local s _c _is_cyc _is_par _pg
1071	        for s in "${cs[@]}"; do
1072	            _is_cyc=0; _is_par=0
1073	            for _c in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do [[ "$_c" == "$s" ]] && { _is_cyc=1; break; }; done
1074	            for _pg in "${_TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS[@]}"; do [[ "$_pg" == "$s" ]] && { _is_par=1; break; }; done
1075	            [[ $_is_cyc -eq 1 || $_is_par -eq 1 ]] && continue
1076	            if [[ -n "${seen_stage[$s]:-}" ]]; then
1077	                error "cycle '$cid': stage '$s' is in another cycle (cycles must not overlap)"
1078	                return 1
1079	            fi
1080	            seen_stage[$s]=1
1081	        done
1082	        local first_pos=-1 last_pos=-1 pos i
1083	        while IFS= read -r s; do
1084	            [[ -n "$s" ]] || continue
1085	            pos=-1
1086	            for i in "${!_TPL_STAGES[@]}"; do
1087	                [[ "${_TPL_STAGES[$i]}" == "$s" ]] && { pos=$i; break; }
1088	            done
1089	            if [[ $pos -eq -1 ]]; then
1090	                error "cycle '$cid': stage '$s' not in template stages[]"
1091	                return 1
1092	            fi
1093	            if [[ $first_pos -ne -1 && $pos -ne $((last_pos + 1)) ]]; then
1094	                error "cycle '$cid': stages must be a contiguous subsequence of template stages[]"
1095	                return 1
1096	            fi
1097	            [[ $first_pos -eq -1 ]] && first_pos=$pos
1098	            last_pos=$pos
1099	        done < <(_tpl_flow_leaves "$cid")
1100	
1101	        # Top-level loops must not overlap each other; a nested loop lies inside
1102	        # its outer loop's range by construction.
1103	        local _nested_in=0 _oc _ov
1104	        for _oc in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do
1105	            _ov="_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_${_oc//-/_}"
1106	            [[ ",${!_ov:-}," == *",$cid,"* ]] && { _nested_in=1; break; }
1107	        done
1108	        if [[ $_nested_in -eq 0 && $first_pos -ne -1 ]]; then
1109	            if [[ $first_pos -le $prev_end ]]; then
1110	                error "cycle '$cid': overlaps a previously declared cycle"
1111	                return 1
1112	            fi
1113	            prev_end=$last_pos
1114	        fi
1115	
1116	        # max_iterations required + bounded
1117	        local max_var="_TPL_CYCLE_MAX_${safe}"
1118	        local max="${!max_var:-}"
1119	        if [[ -z "$max" ]] || ! [[ "$max" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$max" -lt 1 ]] || [[ "$max" -gt 10 ]]; then
1120	            error "cycle '$cid': max_iterations required integer in 1..10, got: ${max:-<unset>}"
1121	            return 1
1122	        fi
1123	
1124	        # #840 scope_policy enum validation (ADR-030). All fields optional;
1125	        # absent ⇒ safe defaults already applied by the consumer. When present,
1126	        # values MUST be from the closed vocabularies — the template names
1127	        # behaviors, it cannot express logic.
1128	        local sx_var="_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_EXPANDABLE_${safe}"; local sx="${!sx_var:-false}"
1129	        if [[ "$sx" != "true" && "$sx" != "false" ]]; then
1130	            error "cycle '$cid': scope_policy.expandable must be true|false, got: $sx"
1131	            return 1
1132	        fi
1133	        local sag_var="_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_AUTO_GRANT_${safe}"; local sag="${!sag_var:-}"
1134	        if [[ -n "$sag" ]]; then
1135	            local _cls
1136	            local _save_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=','
1137	            # shellcheck disable=SC2206
1138	            local -a _classes=($sag)
1139	            IFS="$_save_ifs"
1140	            for _cls in "${_classes[@]}"; do
1141	                case "$_cls" in
1142	                    collateral_tests|collateral_config|collateral_docs|structural) : ;;
1143	                    *) error "cycle '$cid': scope_policy.auto_grant unknown class '$_cls' (valid: collateral_tests, collateral_config, collateral_docs, structural)"; return 1 ;;
1144	                esac
1145	            done
1146	        fi
1147	        local sesc_var="_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_ESCALATE_${safe}"; local sesc="${!sesc_var:-none}"
1148	        case "$sesc" in structural|none) : ;; *) error "cycle '$cid': scope_policy.escalate must be structural|none, got: $sesc"; return 1 ;; esac
1149	        local sod_var="_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_ON_DENY_${safe}"; local sod="${!sod_var:-abandon}"
1150	        case "$sod" in abandon) : ;; *) error "cycle '$cid': scope_policy.on_deny must be abandon, got: $sod"; return 1 ;; esac
1151	
1152	        # #1284 (ADR-047): multi-condition exit_when replaces the single-condition
1153	        # UNTIL vars. When a combinator is present, validate the N conditions at
1154	        # this preflight layer (mirroring the runtime check in cycle-orchestrator.sh
1155	        # _cycle_load_template); otherwise validate the single-condition until.stage.
1156	        local ew_comb_check_var="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR_${safe}"
1157	        local ew_comb="${!ew_comb_check_var:-}"
1158	        if [[ -n "$ew_comb" ]]; then
1159	            case "$ew_comb" in
1160	                all|any) : ;;
1161	                *) error "cycle '$cid': exit_when combinator must be all|any, got: $ew_comb"; return 1 ;;
1162	            esac
1163	            local ew_count_var="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_COUNT_${safe}"
1164	            local ew_count="${!ew_count_var:-}"
1165	            if [[ -z "$ew_count" ]] || ! [[ "$ew_count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$ew_count" -lt 1 ]]; then
1166	                error "cycle '$cid': exit_when multi-condition count must be integer >=1, got: ${ew_count:-<unset>}"
1167	                return 1
1168	            fi
1169	            local ew_i
1170	            for (( ew_i=1; ew_i<=ew_count; ew_i++ )); do
1171	                local _sv="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_${ew_i}_STAGE_${safe}"
1172	                local _fv="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_${ew_i}_FIELD_${safe}"
1173	                local _ov="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_${ew_i}_OP_${safe}"
1174	                local _vv="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_${ew_i}_VALUE_${safe}"
1175	                local ew_s="${!_sv:-}" ew_f="${!_fv:-}" ew_o="${!_ov:-}" ew_v="${!_vv:-}"
1176	                if [[ -z "$ew_s" || -z "$ew_f" || -z "$ew_o" || -z "$ew_v" ]]; then
1177	                    error "cycle '$cid': exit_when condition $ew_i: {stage,field,op,value} all required"
1178	                    return 1
1179	                fi
1180	                case "$ew_f" in
1181	                    verdict|status) : ;;
1182	                    *) error "cycle '$cid': exit_when condition $ew_i: field must be verdict|status, got: $ew_f"; return 1 ;;
1183	                esac
1184	                case "$ew_o" in
1185	                    eq|ne|in) : ;;
1186	                    *) error "cycle '$cid': exit_when condition $ew_i: op must be eq|ne|in, got: $ew_o"; return 1 ;;
1187	                esac
1188	                local found=0
1189	                for s in "${cs[@]}"; do
1190	                    [[ "$s" == "$ew_s" ]] && found=1 && break
1191	                done
1192	                if [[ $found -ne 1 ]]; then
1193	                    error "cycle '$cid': exit_when condition $ew_i: stage '$ew_s' is not in cycle stages (${cs[*]})"
1194	                    return 1
1195	                fi
1196	            done
