content.content:
1	id: simple
2	name: Simple Pipeline
3	extends: null
4	
5	# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
6	merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged
7	
8	defaults:
9	  strategy: map
10	
11	# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
12	# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
13	# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses, review-aggregator,
14	# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
15	# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
16	#
17	# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
18	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
19	# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
20	# mechanical gates + gate-aggregator; the objective-gate plugin was then removed
21	# in B7 (#1139). The single merge-blocking construct is the gate-aggregator
22	# verdict (ADR-040 §5), reached via the cycle's exit_when.
23	#
24	# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
25	# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
26	# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
27	# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
28	# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
29	# one work unit per lens element — followed by
30	# `review-aggregator`, which merges the per-lens results into ONE advisory
31	# merge-readiness report. The lens group is ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
32	# exit_when/convergence (that remains the gate-aggregator, ADR-040 §5) and never
33	# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
34	flow:
35	  - hydrate
36	  - intake
37	  - plan
38	  - delivery_loop
39	  - review_lenses
40	  - review-aggregator
41	  - pr
42	
43	# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
45	# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
46	#
47	# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
48	# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
49	# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
50	# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
51	# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
52	# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
53	# called.
54	#
55	# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
56	# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
57	# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
58	#
59	# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
60	# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
61	# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
62	# quietly running nothing.
63	always_run:
64	  - release
65	  - persist
66	
67	# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
68	# One outer loop holds the design loop and the build loop. Every stage sees
69	# every finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine
70	# never decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
71	#   - A design loop that runs out of rounds ends this round (build is skipped)
72	#     and this loop goes round. When this loop's rounds are spent, the run stops.
73	delivery_loop:
74	  type: cycle
75	  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
76	  flow:
77	    - design_verify_cycle
78	    - build_test_cycle
79	  exit_when:
80	    all:
81	      - { stage: design_verify_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
82	      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
83	  max_iterations: 2
84	  on_max: halt
85	
86	# ─── design_verify_cycle (cycle) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
87	# ADR-046 (#1218, EPIC #1216): give the design stage an independent verifier that
88	# loops back TO it BEFORE the build cycle — so design/contract defects are caught
89	# where they are authored, not deep in the build cycle. Modelled on standard.yaml's
90	# design_impact_cycle (standard.yaml:40-67), which simple.yaml historically lacked.
91	#
92	# Members: design → design-gate. design-gate is a T0 tool (ADR-037 §3): a pure-grep
93	# PRE-build structural gate over design.md + the red-first stubs design writes. It
94	# is BOTH a cycle member AND convergence:gate, so the typed-aggregator preflight
95	# rule (A) is satisfied by binding exit_when directly to it — a single gate, no
96	# separate aggregator needed (contrast build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator, which
97	# rolls up MANY gates). exit_when fires on design-gate.verdict == pass.
98	# max_iterations: 2, on_max: halt (#2176): a contract the gate still rejects is
99	# not built. Nested in delivery_loop (#2271), running out of rounds ends that
100	# loop's round — build is skipped — and the outer loop goes round.
101	#
102	# Feedback: design.design → design.prior_design (self-edge) — mirrors
103	# design_impact_cycle so iter N+1 refines rather than re-creates (#773 lesson).
104	#
105	design_verify_cycle:
106	  type: cycle
107	  description: Verify the design contract is build-ready until design-gate passes
108	  flow:
109	    - design
110	    # #1683: does the design cover what the ISSUE asked for? Design is the only
111	    # reader of the issue, so nothing else confirms the SPECs are a faithful
112	    # statement of the ask. Inside the cycle, so a finding reaches design itself
113	    # on the next iteration.
114	    - spec-coverage
115	    - design-gate
116	  # #1284/ADR-047 multi-condition: BOTH must hold. spec-coverage may gate under
117	  # ADR-040 §5 as amended by #2040 — the standard it judges against is the
118	  # ISSUE, which design cannot re-author, so the only way to converge is to
119	  # actually cover it.
120	  #
121	  # `ne uncovered` rather than `eq covered`: `unreadable` must not stall the
122	  # cycle. intake writes a placeholder when the issue fetch fails (#1804), and
123	  # failing closed there would break every offline run for a condition that is
124	  # not design's fault. The finding still ships in the summary.
125	  exit_when:
126	    all:
127	      - { stage: design-gate, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
128	      - { stage: spec-coverage, field: verdict, op: ne, value: uncovered }
129	  max_iterations: 2
130	  on_max: halt
131	
132	# ─── spec-coverage (leaf, gate) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
133	# Model-judged but admissible on the convergence path (ADR-040 §5 / #2040): its
134	# standard is the issue, produced by intake OUTSIDE this cycle, so the judged
135	# party cannot re-author it.
136	spec-coverage:
137	  gate: auto
138	  roles: [spec_coverage]
139	  # A product owner asks "was what was asked for delivered?" — intent-seeking,
140	  # which is wrong for judging an assertion against a SPEC (the bug there
141	  # survives charity) and exactly right here, where the question IS about intent.
142	  persona: product-owner
143	  stage_timeout_s: 600
144	  router:
145	    timeout_s: 600
146	
147	# ─── test-author (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────────────
148	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
149	# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
150	# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
151	test-author:
152	  gate: auto
153	  roles: [test_author]
154	  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
155	  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
156	  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
157	  blocking: true
158	  stage_timeout_s: 900
159	  router:
160	    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
161	    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
162	    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
163	    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
164	    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
165	    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
166	    timeout_s: 900
167	    max_turns: 0
168	    max_iterations: 4
169	
170	# ─── spec-correspondence (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────
171	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not gate. Its finding reaches
172	# test-author on the next iteration through the summary channel.
173	spec-correspondence:
174	  gate: auto
175	  roles: [spec_correspondence]
176	  # #1627: personas were consumed only by review lenses and NO template carried
177	  # a persona: key, so a persona manifest resolved to nothing. This is the first
178	  # stage-level binding. QA assures traceability; it does not test — which is
179	  # what separates it from test-strategist, whose instinct shown a mismatched
180	  # assertion is to repair it and answer yes.
181	  persona: quality-assurance
182	  stage_timeout_s: 600
183	  router:
184	    timeout_s: 600
185	
186	# ─── assertion-integrity (leaf, gate) ────────────────────────────────────────
187	# Mechanical, no model.route — so it MAY gate (ADR-040 §5).
188	assertion-integrity:
189	  gate: auto
190	  roles: [assertion_integrity]
191	  stage_timeout_s: 600
192	
193	# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
194	# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
195	# path is allowed for the same reason as spec-coverage (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
196	# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
197	issue-acceptance:
198	  gate: auto
199	  roles: [issue_acceptance]
200	  # Same question spec-coverage asks of the design — "was what was asked for
201	  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
202	  persona: product-owner
203	  stage_timeout_s: 600
204	  router:
205	    timeout_s: 600
206	
207	# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
208	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
209	# mechanical gates (shape-floor, acceptance-gate, secret-scan) and finally the
210	# gate-aggregator, which collapses every must-pass gate into ONE convergence
211	# verdict. exit_when fires on gate-aggregator.verdict == pass — the ADR-019
212	# fail-closed contract re-expressed as a single composable construct (ADR-040 §5).
213	# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
214	# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
215	# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
216	# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
217	# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
218	# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
219	# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
220	# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
221	# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
222	# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
223	# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
224	# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
225	# which goes round from design.
226	build_test_cycle:
227	  type: cycle
228	  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until gate-aggregator passes
229	  flow:
230	    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
231	    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
232	    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
233	    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff.
234	    - test-author
235	    # #2034: judges whether each assertion tests what its SPEC SAYS — the one
236	    # link execution cannot reach (a passing test proves the implementation
237	    # satisfies the ASSERTION, never that the assertion satisfies the SENTENCE).
238	    # Before build, because its question needs the requirement and the assertion
239	    # and not the implementation — which at this point does not exist yet, so
240	    # its isolation is a fact of placement rather than a rule to enforce.
241	    - spec-correspondence
242	    - build
243	    - test
244	    - shape-floor
245	    - acceptance-gate
246	    - secret-scan
247	    # #2022: mechanical backstop. The spawn denies build Edit() on the declared
248	    # TESTFILES, but #1919 P5 measured that a Write(...) deny rule matches
249	    # nothing — prevention is incomplete by construction. A fail here makes the
250	    # aggregate non-pass, so the cycle iterates rather than converging on a
251	    # rewritten assertion.
252	    - assertion-integrity
253	    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
254	    # only check after spec-coverage that reads the issue at all. A convergence
255	    # gate, so gate-aggregator's roster makes it must-pass; each unmet
256	    # requirement is a numbered finding.
257	    - issue-acceptance
258	    - gate-aggregator
259	  exit_when:
260	    stage: gate-aggregator
261	    field: verdict
262	    op: eq
263	    value: pass
264	  max_iterations: 3
265	  on_max: continue
266	  # The cycle CONVERGES rather than spinning build(no-op)→…→gate-aggregator(fail)
267	  # because the aggregator's consolidated gate-feedback.md reaches build. B2
268	  # (ADR-040): the gate-aggregator is the SINGLE collector of failure detail,
269	  # merging every failing mechanical gate into one document. It used to arrive
270	  # through a feedback: wire plus a bespoke reader; #1979 retired both — the
271	  # aggregator marks that output `summary: true` (#1976) and the engine injects
272	  # it, framed by verdict, with no per-consumer wiring.
273	# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
274	intake:
275	  gate: auto
276	  roles: [intake]
277	  stage_timeout_s: 600
278	  io:
279	    destinations: [file, stdout]
280	    tail_lines: 200
281	
282	# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
283	plan:
284	  gate: auto
285	  roles: [planner]
286	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
287	  persona: product-owner
288	  stage_timeout_s: 1200
289	  io:
290	    destinations: [file, stdout]
291	    tail_lines: 200
292	  router:
293	    timeout_s: 300
294	    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442): scope exploration needs
295	    # headroom. The planner is
296	    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
297	    max_turns: 45
298	
299	# ─── design (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ───────────────────────────────
300	design:
301	  gate: auto
302	  roles: [designer]
303	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
304	  persona: architect
305	  stage_timeout_s: 3900
306	  io:
307	    destinations: [file, stdout]
308	    tail_lines: 200
309	  router:
310	    timeout_s: 600
311	    max_turns: 0
312	
313	# ─── design-gate (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ──────────────────────────
314	# T0 tool gate (ADR-046, #1218): PRE-build mechanical structural gate. Pure grep
315	# over design.md (NO LLM, NO baseline — ADR-037 §3). Runs the 5 structural
316	# checks (scope non-empty; acceptance block well-formed; every SPEC has a status
317	# — [code], [no-code] or [done] with evidence that exists (ADR-069); every [code]
318	# SPEC declares a TESTFILE; WIRING present/none + paths exist) and reports ALL
319	# violations in ONE pass. verdict-in-artifact; the design_verify_cycle exit_when
320	# reads design-gate.verdict == pass. Bound by role design_gate.
321	design-gate:
322	  gate: auto
323	  roles: [design_gate]
324	  stage_timeout_s: 600
325	  io:
326	    destinations: [file, stdout]
327	    tail_lines: 200
328	
329	# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
330	build:
331	  gate: auto
332	  roles: [builder]
333	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
334	  persona: developer
335	  stage_timeout_s: 4200
336	  io:
337	    destinations: [file, stdout]
338	    tail_lines: 200
339	  router:
340	    timeout_s: 900
341	    max_turns: 0
342	
343	# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
344	test:
345	  gate: auto
346	  roles: [tester]
347	  stage_timeout_s: 5400
348	  io:
349	    destinations: [file, stdout]
350	    tail_lines: 200
351	
352	# ─── shape-floor (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
353	# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1134): un-gameable shape-floor check. verdict-in-artifact.
354	shape-floor:
355	  gate: auto
356	  roles: [shape_floor]
357	  stage_timeout_s: 600
358	  io:
359	    destinations: [file, stdout]
360	    tail_lines: 200
361	
362	# ─── acceptance-gate (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
363	# Mechanical (non-LLM) acceptance-contract gate (ADR-036, #922). No-op pass when
364	# the design acceptance block is absent (its design input is required:false in the
365	# manifest — design already emits the SPEC/WIRING block). Its gate_result feeds
366	# the acceptance→build feedback edge above.
367	# ADR-036 #1188: negctl_timeout_s bounds each SPEC negative-control / reachability
368	# test run (seconds). A timeout is classified INFRA (non-terminal), never a
369	# violation. Override per-run with ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT (env wins).
370	acceptance-gate:
371	  gate: auto
372	  roles: [acceptance_gate]
373	  negctl_timeout_s: 60
374	  stage_timeout_s: 600
375	  io:
376	    destinations: [file, stdout]
377	    tail_lines: 200
378	  router:
379	    timeout_s: 600
380	    max_turns: 10
381	
382	# ─── secret-scan (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
383	# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1136): blocks hardcoded secrets/.env in the diff.
384	# verdict-in-artifact (skip on empty diff).
385	secret-scan:
386	  gate: auto
387	  roles: [secret_scan]
388	  stage_timeout_s: 600
389	  io:
390	    destinations: [file, stdout]
391	    tail_lines: 200
392	
393	# ─── gate-aggregator (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
394	# T0 convergence aggregator (ADR-040 §2/§5, #1137): collapses the must-pass gate
395	# set into ONE verdict. This is the cycle's exit_when source and the single
396	# merge-blocking construct in the decomposed pipeline. verdict-in-artifact.
397	gate-aggregator:
398	  gate: auto
399	  roles: [gate_aggregator]
400	  stage_timeout_s: 600
401	  io:
402	    destinations: [file, stdout]
403	    tail_lines: 200
404	
405	# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
406	# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
407	# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
408	# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
409	# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
410	# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
411	# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
412	# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
413	# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
414	#
415	# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
416	# Convergence is owned by the build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator exit_when above;
417	# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
418	review_lenses:
419	  type: map
420	  over: lenses
421	  # ADR-051 §2: each lens names the persona it runs as; none is inferred
422	  # from the lens's name.
423	  elements:
424	    - id: security
425	      persona: security
426	    - id: performance
427	      persona: performance
428	    - id: red-team
429	      persona: red-team
430	    - id: correctness
431	      persona: correctness
432	    - id: scope
433	      persona: scope
434	    - id: sre
435	      persona: sre
436	  roles: [review_lens]
437	  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
438	  max_parallel: 4
439	  on_member_error: continue
440	  aggregate: advisory
441	  stage_timeout_s: 600
442	  io:
443	    destinations: [file]
444	    tail_lines: 200
445	  router:
446	    timeout_s: 300
447	    max_turns: 25
448	
449	# ─── review-aggregator (leaf, ADVISORY) ──────────────────────────────────────
450	# C2 (#1141, ADR-040 §3/§4): merges the review_lenses members' results — the
451	# lens_result set the engine hands it (ADR-055 §1.4, #1842) — into ONE advisory
452	# merge-readiness report (review-report.json + review-report.md). Does NO LLM call
453	# — it merges lens JSON only. Bound by role review_aggregator to
454	# plugins/agent/review-aggregator. Requires lens_result: with no lens result the
455	# engine refuses it, and an empty set reports needs_attention, never "ready"
456	# (#1753). Never recommends a merge action, never blocks.
457	# The report.json filename is unchanged, so merge / pr-delivery consume it as before.
458	review-aggregator:
459	  gate: auto
460	  roles: [review_aggregator]
461	  stage_timeout_s: 600
462	  io:
463	    destinations: [file, stdout]
464	    tail_lines: 200
465	
466	# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
467	# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
468	pr:
469	  gate: auto
470	  roles: [pr]
471	  stage_timeout_s: 600
472	  io:
473	    destinations: [file, stdout]
474	    tail_lines: 200
475	
476	# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
477	# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
478	# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
479	# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
480	# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
481	#
482	# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
483	# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
484	# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
485	release:
486	  gate: auto
487	  roles: [teardown]
488	  stage_timeout_s: 30
489	  io:
490	    destinations: [file]
491	    tail_lines: 50
492	
493	# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
494	# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
495	# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
496	# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
497	# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
498	# abort.
499	#
500	# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
501	# process-group kill does not.
502	persist:
503	  gate: auto
504	  roles: [persist]
505	  stage_timeout_s: 120
506	  io:
507	    destinations: [file]
508	    tail_lines: 50
509	
510	# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
511	# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
512	# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
513	# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
514	#
515	# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
516	# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
517	# an earlier push never delivered.
518	hydrate:
519	  gate: auto
520	  roles: [hydrate]
521	  stage_timeout_s: 600
522	  router:
523	    timeout_s: 60
524	  io:
525	    destinations: [file]
526	    tail_lines: 50

## Summary

I've retrieved all six requested files. Here's what each file contains:

**1. `/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh` (631 lines)**
Core plugin dispatch and lifecycle management. Owns `plugin_hook_call` (dispatches plugin hooks in isolated subshells with timeout enforcement) and `scan_plugin_outputs` (fail-closed artifact validation per ADR-001). Handles stage dispatch context setup, write-boundary enforcement, input resolution, and watchdog timeouts for long-running stages.

**2. `/core/pipeline/runner.sh` (3983 lines, reading lines 1-1227)**
Main pipeline orchestrator. Defines the runner interface, stage execution loop, artifact snapshotting, process group teardown, and exit-status handling. Contains helpers for template loading, preflight validation, leaf-stage resolvability, and pipeline-end rendering. Critical for understanding the overall execution flow and timeout mechanisms.

**3. `/core/orch/local_engine.sh` (190 lines)**
Shared dispatch/collect/shutdown backend for local orchestrators. Provides abstraction for dispatching work units in background subshells, polling for completion with timeouts, and graceful shutdown (TERM → grace period → KILL).

**4. `/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh` (164 lines)**
Process group resolution and kill helpers. Defines `zbuild_pg_resolve`, `zbuild_pg_kill`, `zbuild_pid_kill`, and related utilities for managing process groups across POSIX platforms (Linux/macOS). Implements TERM-then-KILL escalation with configurable grace periods.

Template loading and stage resolution engine. Parses YAML pipeline templates (new ADR-027 and legacy v2 shapes), manages stage metadata, cycle/parallel/map group definitions, and dispatch unit generation. Validates template structure, stage dependencies, and cycle acyclicity.

**6. `/config/templates/simple.yaml` (527 lines)**
Example pipeline template defining a 7-stage flow: hydrate → intake → plan → delivery_loop (with nested design_verify_cycle and build_test_cycle) → review_lenses → review-aggregator → pr, plus always-run teardown stages (release, persist). Template includes per-stage configuration, io/router settings, personas, and cycle exit conditions.

All files are ready for your design document scope and acceptance spec.

4	# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

7	# `plugin_hook_call` (sources plugin.sh in an isolated subshell, applies
8	# pre-source tamper checks, calls the hook function, then verifies declared
9	# outputs) and `scan_plugin_outputs` (ADR-001 fail-closed artifact-presence
10	# scanner). Depends on yaml_get / verify_plugin_for_source from the other two
11	# split modules — sourced together via the registry.sh facade.
12	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail.
13	
14	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
15	_ZBUILD_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE_LOADED=1
16	
17	# #1809 (ADR-058 C9): declared-output path resolution is shared with
18	# core/pipeline/write-boundary.sh so the artifact scanner and the write-boundary
19	# classifier can never disagree about where a declared output lives.

29	# ─── scan_plugin_outputs — fail-closed artifact-presence scanner (#288) ─────
30	# ADR-001 §Fail-closed scanner contract:
31	#   "If a plugin declares an output but no artifact exists at outputs[].path
32	#    after run completes with exit 0, the engine emits a synthetic blocking
33	#    finding."
34	# #1906 retired provides.artifact_type, which the original wording keyed on;
35	# outputs[].required is the single declaration the scan now honours.
36	#
37	# Arguments:
38	#   $1 — plugin_dir
39	#   $2 — state_file (so $state_dir / $artifacts_dir can substitute into paths)
40	#
41	# Returns:
42	#   0 if all declared outputs are present (or no outputs declared).
43	#   1 if any declared output is missing — and emits one
44	#      `plugin.artifact.missing` event per missing path.
45	#
46	# Path-template substitution (Phase 0.5): supports ${state_dir} and
47	# ${artifact_dir} / ${artifacts_dir}. Any other ${VAR} resolves from the work
48	# unit's exported environment (#1803) — per-member outputs such as review-lens's
49	# `lens-${ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID}.json` (ADR-047 §2) are only checkable once the
50	# element var is expanded. A var that is unset stays literal and fails the check.
51	scan_plugin_outputs() {
52	    local plugin_dir="$1"
53	    local state_file="${2:-}"
54	    local stage="${3:-}"
55	    # #2252: `probe` answers present-or-not with no events, findings or marker.
56	    local probe="${4:-}"
57	    local manifest="$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
58	
59	    # No manifest, no outputs to scan — silently succeed.
60	    [[ ! -f "$manifest" ]] && return 0
61	
62	    local plugin_id; plugin_id="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "id" 2>/dev/null || true)"
63	    local kind; kind="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "kind" 2>/dev/null || true)"
64	    # ADR-047 §4 capability flag: build legitimately writes a zero-byte diff.patch
65	    # when a turn changed no code. The exemption is deliberately narrow — it never
66	    # covers a `primary: true` output, so a stage cannot mask an empty verdict
67	    # artifact (e.g. build-summary.json) by declaring the flag in its own manifest.
68	    local empty_diff_ok; empty_diff_ok="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "capabilities.empty_diff_legitimate" 2>/dev/null || true)"
69	
70	    # Compute substitution roots from state_file.
71	    local state_dir="" artifact_dir=""
72	    if [[ -n "$state_file" ]]; then
73	        state_dir="$(dirname "$state_file")"
74	        artifact_dir="${state_dir}/artifacts"
75	    fi
76	
77	    # Pull outputs[].path entries from the manifest. yaml_get/yaml_get_list
78	    # don't model lists of objects, so grep the YAML directly. Format we
79	    # support (per ADR-001):
80	    #   outputs:
81	    #     - name: foo
82	    #       path: ${artifact_dir}/foo.json
83	    #       type: foo.json
84	    # #511 F2: respect `required: false` on outputs. Without this, the scanner
85	    # would flag a legitimately optional artifact as a fail-closed contract
86	    # violation. (test_failures_summary was the original example; ADR-055 §9
87	    # since made it `required: true` — a summary is published on every terminal
88	    # verdict, so its absence IS a violation now.)
89	    local paths
90	    paths="$(_registry_output_path_rows "$manifest")"
91	
92	    [[ -z "$paths" ]] && return 0
93	
94	    local missing=0
95	    local raw_path raw_primary resolved _violation _event
96	    while IFS=$'\t' read -r raw_path raw_primary; do
97	        [[ -z "$raw_path" ]] && continue
98	        resolved="$(_registry_resolve_output_path "$raw_path" "$state_dir" "$artifact_dir")"
99	
100	        # An absent output always violates; a zero-byte one violates unless the
101	        # plugin declared the empty-diff capability AND this is not its primary.
102	        _violation=""
103	        if [[ ! -e "$resolved" ]]; then
104	            _violation="absent"
105	            _event="plugin.artifact.missing"
106	        elif [[ ! -s "$resolved" ]] &&
107	             ! { [[ "$empty_diff_ok" == "true" ]] && [[ "$raw_primary" != "true" ]]; }; then
108	            _violation="empty"
109	            _event="plugin.artifact.empty"
110	        fi
111	
112	        if [[ -n "$_violation" && "$probe" == "probe" ]]; then
113	            return 1
114	        fi
115	        if [[ -n "$_violation" ]]; then
116	            if [[ "$_violation" == "absent" ]]; then
117	                error "scan_plugin_outputs: plugin=$plugin_id declared output missing: $resolved (template: $raw_path)"
118	            else
119	                error "scan_plugin_outputs: plugin=$plugin_id declared output is empty (zero bytes): $resolved (template: $raw_path)"
120	            fi
121	            emit_event "$_event" \
122	                "plugin=$plugin_id" \
123	                "kind=$kind" \
124	                "expected_path=$resolved" \
125	                "template=$raw_path"
126	            # ADR-001 §Fail-closed contract: emit plugin.contract.violated and write
127	            # synthetic blocking findings.json so the output stage can surface the violation.
128	            local _stage_id="${stage:-${plugin_id}}"
129	            emit_event "plugin.contract.violated" \
130	                "stage=$_stage_id" \
131	                "plugin=$plugin_id" \
132	                "expected_path=$resolved" \
133	                "reason=artifact_missing_or_empty"
134	            if [[ -n "$state_dir" ]]; then
135	                mkdir -p "${state_dir}/artifacts"
136	                local _findings_file="${state_dir}/artifacts/${_stage_id}-${plugin_id}-contract-violated-findings.json"
137	                jq -n \
138	                    --arg stage "$_stage_id" \
139	                    --arg plugin "$plugin_id" \
140	                    --arg path "$resolved" \
141	                    --arg violation "$_violation" \
142	                    '{
143	                        schema_version: 1,
144	                        findings: [{
145	                            id: "artifact-contract-violated",
146	                            title: ("Plugin contract violated: " + $plugin +
147	                                    (if $violation == "empty"
148	                                     then " wrote an empty (zero-byte) required output"
149	                                     else " declared a required output but wrote no artifact" end)),
150	                            severity: "blocking",
151	                            stage: $stage,
152	                            plugin: $plugin,
153	                            detail: ("Expected artifact at: " + $path)
154	                        }]
155	                    }' > "$_findings_file" 2>/dev/null || true
156	                # #1809: file-backed marker so runner_read_stage_disposition (a separate
157	                # process under map:) can detect the violation and return broken.
158	                mkdir -p "${state_dir}/runtime"
159	                touch "${state_dir}/runtime/artifact-contract-violated" 2>/dev/null || true
160	            fi
161	            missing=$((missing + 1))
162	        fi
163	    done <<< "$paths"
164	
165	    return $((missing > 0))
166	}

168	# ─── _lc_owned_by_others_deny <state_dir> <stage> (#2189) ────────────────────
169	# One absolute path per line: every file a stage OTHER than <stage> reported
170	# owning (artifacts/stage-reports.json). Empty when nothing is owned.
171	_lc_owned_by_others_deny() {
172	    local rec="${1:-}/artifacts/stage-reports.json" me="${2:-}"
173	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || return 0
174	    # Read without a fork: nothing owned (most runs) needs no jq at all.
175	    local _body; _body="$(<"$rec")"
176	    [[ "$_body" == *'"owned_files"'* ]] || return 0
177	    jq -r --arg me "$me" --arg root "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-.}" '
178	        [(.owned_files // {}) | to_entries[] | select(.key != $me) | .value[] | "\($root)/\(.)"]
179	        | unique[]' <<< "$_body" 2>/dev/null
180	}

182	# ─── plugin_hook_call ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
183	# Source the plugin's plugin.sh and call a lifecycle hook by name.
184	# Plugin functions are isolated by sub-shell to prevent namespace pollution.
185	plugin_hook_call() {
186	    local plugin_dir="$1"
187	    local hook_name="$2"   # run | cleanup (or kind-specific)
188	    shift 2
189	    local manifest="$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
190	    local plugin_sh="$plugin_dir/plugin.sh"
191	
192	    # ADR-068 §8: mark when this run of the stage started, FIRST — before any
193	    # refusal below can return — so a run that writes no result, refused or
194	    # not, is never credited with the previous run's (stage_result_is_current).
195	    [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && stage_dispatch_mark "${2:-}" "${1:-}"
196	
197	    if [[ ! -f "$plugin_sh" ]]; then
198	        error "plugin_hook_call: plugin.sh missing: $plugin_sh"

200	    fi

202	    local plugin_id; plugin_id="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "id")"
203	    local kind; kind="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "kind")"
204	
205	    # ADR-054 §3 (#1862): the engine states, for exactly the span of one
206	    # dispatch, which stage this is and which plugin serves it.
207	    #
208	    # A plugin IS self-defining about what it is — plugin-bootstrap.sh resolves
209	    # _ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR from its own BASH_SOURCE, and 18 plugins do. It can
210	    # never be self-defining about which STAGE it is: `review_lenses`
211	    # (simple.yaml) is served by plugin `review-lens` via role `review_lens` —
212	    # three namespaces the template alone maps, and under `map:` all six lens
213	    # members receive that one stage name. Everything keyed to the flow (the
214	    # timeline, stage_statuses, the per-stage router knobs) needs the stage
215	    # name; introspection can only ever yield the plugin id.
216	    #
217	    # `local -x`, not `export`, for three reasons: it reaches the emit_event
218	    # calls below, which fire OUTSIDE the plugin subshell (the blank envelope
219	    # .plugin/.kind of #1705); it reaches the subshell and anything it spawns;
220	    # and it unsets on return, so stage N's identity cannot bleed into stage
221	    # N+1 — a plain export would trade a blank field for a stale one.
222	    #
223	    # This is the only site that reaches all four dispatch arms. The `map:` arm
224	    # runs a generated standalone script (strategies/common.sh) the runner
225	    # cannot export into — but plugin_hook_call is its last line.
226	    #
227	    # ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT is deliberately NOT set: it is an operator override
228	    # every reader spells `${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-<default>}`, and ADR-024 /
229	    # persona-resolve.sh forbid relying on it as a root. Derive from
230	    # ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR instead.
231	    #
232	    # Stage id is $1 post-shift for both hooks — run(stage_id, state_file, ...)

234	    # scan_plugin_outputs already makes below.
235	    #
236	    # `:-` is deliberate and deliberately unlike `stage_arg="${1:-}"` below: an
237	    # empty $1 keeps the ambient stage rather than blanking it. A caller with no
238	    # stage to name must not erase the one its own caller established — the
239	    # throttle marker's path is keyed on this value and is written inside the
240	    # dispatch but read outside it (router-rc-classify.sh:154), so a blank here
241	    # would split the key across the boundary. scan_plugin_outputs has no such
242	    # cross-boundary reader and wants the literal argument.
243	    local -x ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE="${1:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
244	    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): the unit's own name — the stage, or <stage>.<element>
245	    # for a map member — for this dispatch only. The element is consumed here, so
246	    # a stage dispatched from inside the member is named by its own stage.
247	    local -x ZBUILD_UNIT="${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE}${ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT:+.${ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT}}"
248	    local -x ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT=""
249	    local -x ZBUILD_PLUGIN="$plugin_id"
250	    local -x ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND="$kind"
251	    local -x ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR="$plugin_dir"
252	
253	    # ADR-058 §2 (#1918): the engine states WHERE this stage may write, for
254	    # exactly the span of one dispatch. #1809 makes a declared output a write
255	    # boundary; a boundary cannot be enforced until the permitted areas are
256	    # defined, and the per-stage scratch area did not exist at all.
257	    #
258	    # Same site and same `local -x` as the identity block above, for the same
259	    # reasons: it is the only site reaching all four dispatch arms (the `map:`
260	    # arm runs a generated standalone script the runner cannot export into, and
261	    # this call is that script's last line), and `local -x` restores the prior
262	    # value AND the prior export attribute on return, so stage N's scratch
263	    # cannot bleed into stage N+1 and the test harness's sandboxed
264	    # ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR (scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh) comes back intact.
265	    #
266	    # Guarded on `$2` being an ABSOLUTE path — the state_file, post-shift, per
267	    # ADR-054 §2, the same argument scan_plugin_outputs reads below.
268	    #
269	    # Absolute, not merely non-empty, and the difference is load-bearing.
270	    # `dirname` of a bare relative name is `.`, and by the time a stage
271	    # dispatches, the runner has cd'd into the RUN'S WORKTREE (ADR-052) — so a
272	    # relative state_file would put `scratch/` and `artifacts/` inside the
273	    # repository under change. That is the exact leak this block exists to close,
274	    # reintroduced by the block itself.
275	    #
276	    # It cannot happen from the engine: runner.sh absolutizes state_dir "BEFORE
277	    # anything derives a path from state_dir" precisely so no caller has to think
278	    # about this (ADR-052, #1640). A relative or empty `$2` therefore means an
279	    # ad-hoc caller — the `plugin_hook_call … ""` of
280	    # tests/unit/plugin-lifecycle-event-balance-test.sh, or the positional
281	    # `… "arg1" "arg2"` of tests/integration/core-plugin-registry-test.sh — which
282	    # has no job folder to be inside and must reach the plugin with the
283	    # environment it has today.
284	    #

286	    # wildcard-unsets every ZBUILD_* before each model spawn — with the
287	    # unset-until-gone loop #1873 added specifically to defeat `local -x`
288	    # layering at this seam — while TMPDIR is explicitly PRESERVED. It is

290	    # model's own temp writes in bounds and relocates every `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}`

292	    #

294	    # for a live state file first and only fall back to temp when invoked
295	    # ad-hoc, so their outputs land correctly today. What changes is that the
296	    # plugin's own fallback and scan_plugin_outputs' `${artifact_dir}`

299	    if [[ "${2:-}" == /* ]]; then
300	        local _ws_state_dir; _ws_state_dir="$(dirname "$2")"
301	        local -x ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR="${_ws_state_dir}/artifacts"
302	
303	        # #2022: the acceptance TESTFILES belong to the stage that AUTHORS them.

305	        # assertion to agree with its own implementation. Derived from the role
306	        # the plugin declares, never from a stage id: naming `build` here would

308	        # core/router/permissions.sh renders the rules; the decision is here.

310	        # #2170: `$1` here is the STAGE ID — the function `shift 2`s its
311	        # plugin_dir/hook_name arguments away above. Looked up on the stage id
312	        # the role was always empty, so the author was denied its own testfiles
313	        # (invisible while the rule rendered as `Edit(/abs)`, #2163).
314	        # #2189: files ANOTHER stage reported owning (test-author reports the
315	        # testfiles it authored) — from the run's stage-reports record, never
316	        # design.md by path and never a role name. The owner is not denied.

327	            _lc_repo_entries_deny "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-.}"

465	    if declare -F write_boundary_mark >/dev/null 2>&1; then
466	        # Keyed on stage + map element so nested, map and parallel dispatches
467	        # against one state file do not share (and re-stamp) one window.
468	        write_boundary_mark "${2:-}" "${1:-}" "${ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT:-}" || true
469	    fi
470	
471	    # #2186: what the declared outputs were before this run, so the attempt
472	    # record can say which ones the run actually changed. Fail-open.
473	    local _lc_outputs_before=""
474	    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && declare -F attempt_outputs_fingerprint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
475	        _lc_outputs_before="$(attempt_outputs_fingerprint "$plugin_dir" "${2:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
476	    fi
477	
478	    emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.start" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
479	
480	    # Run in a subshell to isolate plugin's variables/functions.
481	    # For the "run" hook: arm a per-dispatch watchdog so a hung stage is killed at
482	    # stage_timeout_s (issue #1801, SPEC-1/SPEC-2). Precedence: template
483	    # _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage> > ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S env > 5400 s default.
484	    local rc=0
485	    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]; then
486	        if ! declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
487	            source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
488	        fi
489	        local _lc_stage_safe="${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE//-/_}"
490	        local _lc_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_${_lc_stage_safe}"
491	        local _lc_hook_to="${!_lc_to_var:-}"
492	        [[ "$_lc_hook_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_lc_hook_to" -gt 0 ]] || _lc_hook_to="${ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S:-5400}"
493	        [[ "$_lc_hook_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_lc_hook_to" -gt 0 ]] || _lc_hook_to=5400
494	        local _lc_hook_pid _lc_wd_pid _lc_m_before=0
495	        [[ "$-" == *m* ]] && _lc_m_before=1
496	        set -m
497	        (
498	            # Always clear monitor mode: the hook subshell is already in its own
499	            # process group (created by set -m + & above). Any background job the
500	            # hook spawns must stay in that group so kill -KILL -- -<pgid> reaches
501	            # them. If the caller had set -m (e.g. _runner_dispatch_always_run's
502	            # outer subshell), the hook would inherit it and its children would get
503	            # their own groups, escaping the KILL (#2333 SPEC-6b).
504	            set +m
505	            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
506	            source "$plugin_sh"
507	            if declare -F "$hook_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
508	                "$hook_fn" "$@"
509	            else
510	                echo "plugin_hook_call: function $hook_fn not defined in $plugin_sh" >&2
511	                exit 1
512	            fi
513	        ) &
514	        _lc_hook_pid=$!
515	        ( set +m; sleep "$_lc_hook_to"; zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true ) &
516	        _lc_wd_pid=$!
517	        set +m
518	        # Restore runner's monitor mode: set +m above always clears it, even when
519	        # ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1 had it enabled before this call.
520	        (( _lc_m_before == 1 )) && set -m
521	        wait "$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
522	        # #2333: the group leader exiting does not mean its group members did.
523	        # A child that ignored TERM would survive if the watchdog is cancelled before
524	        # it delivers KILL, so KILL the whole group now.
525	        kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
526	        declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1 && zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_wd_pid" 1 2>/dev/null || true
527	        wait "$_lc_wd_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
528	        if (( rc == 143 || rc == 137 )); then
529	            emit_event "plugin.run.timed_out" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" \
530	                "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" "timeout_s=${_lc_hook_to}" \
531	                "disposition=timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
532	        fi
533	    else
534	        (
535	            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
536	            source "$plugin_sh"
537	            if declare -F "$hook_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
538	                "$hook_fn" "$@"
539	            else
540	                echo "plugin_hook_call: function $hook_fn not defined in $plugin_sh" >&2
541	                exit 1
542	            fi
543	        )
544	        rc=$?
545	    fi
546	
547	    if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
548	        # #288: after a successful `run`, verify the plugin actually produced
549	        # the artifacts it declared. Absent evidence IS blocking evidence —
550	        # emit synthetic findings for each missing output and surface the
551	        # failure as a non-zero hook exit so the caller can react.
552	        if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]; then
553	            # Per ADR-001 hook signature: $@ after shift 2 is (stage_id, state_file, ...).
554	            local stage_arg="${1:-}"
555	            local state_file_arg="${2:-}"
556	            # #2252: a stage that SAYS it did not finish (timed_out, out_of_turns,
557	            # interrupted) is expected to be missing outputs — failing it for them
558	            # overwrote its retryable word with `broken` and halted the run
559	            # (#1844: design timed out, and the run ended instead of retrying).
560	            # Its own word stands; the retry rule decides what happens next.
561	            # Read the stage's word only when an output IS missing (a quiet
562	            # probe first): the read costs several jq calls per dispatch, and a
563	            # probe that passes means there is nothing for the full check to say.
564	            local _lcr_state="" _lcr_contract="" _lcr_verdict="" _lcr_disp="" _lcr_reason="" \
565	                  _lcr_viol="" _lcr_path="" _lcr_present="" _lc_unfinished="" _lc_missing=0
566	            scan_plugin_outputs "$plugin_dir" "$state_file_arg" "$stage_arg" probe 2>/dev/null || _lc_missing=1
567	            if (( _lc_missing )) && declare -F _verdict_read_result >/dev/null 2>&1 \
568	                    && declare -F disposition_unfinished >/dev/null 2>&1 \
569	                    && [[ -n "$state_file_arg" ]]; then
570	                _verdict_read_result "$(dirname "$state_file_arg")" "$manifest" "$stage_arg" 0 _lcr 2>/dev/null || true
571	                disposition_unfinished "${_lcr_disp:-}" && _lc_unfinished="$_lcr_disp"
572	            fi
573	            if [[ -n "$_lc_unfinished" ]]; then
574	                emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.artifact_check_skipped" "plugin=$plugin_id" \
575	                    "kind=$kind" "disposition=$_lc_unfinished"
576	            elif (( _lc_missing )) && ! scan_plugin_outputs "$plugin_dir" "$state_file_arg" "$stage_arg"; then
577	                emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.artifact_check_failed" \
578	                    "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
579	                # A dispatch that STARTED must also END. This arm and the
580	                # write-boundary arm below both `return 1` from inside the rc=0
581	                # branch, so neither reaches the `complete` emit nor the `else`
582	                # arm's `error` emit — the start was left without a partner and
583	                # the run's own log could not say which stage died (run
584	                # 33899683569: 54 start, 48 complete, 5 error). `reason=` is a
585	                # data field on an already-declared event name, so the event-NAME
586	                # set is unchanged and the sequence goldens are untouched.
587	                emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" \
588	                    "kind=$kind" "rc=1" "reason=artifact-check-failed"
589	                return 1
590	            fi
591	            # #1809 (ADR-058 C9): sweep for writes outside declared outputs and
592	            # engine-owned areas. Fail-open: unloaded module = write_boundary_check
593	            # undefined = this arm is unreachable.
594	            if declare -F write_boundary_check >/dev/null 2>&1; then
595	                _ZBUILD_WB_ACTION=""
596	                if ! write_boundary_check "$plugin_dir" "$state_file_arg" "$stage_arg" \
597	                        "${ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT:-}"; then
598	                    # See the artifact-check arm above: same missing-terminal
599	                    # defect. write_boundary_violation_recorded has already named
600	                    # the offending path on its own three channels; this event
601	                    # is what closes the start/end pair.
602	                    local _wb_reason="write-boundary-violation"
603	                    [[ "${_ZBUILD_WB_ACTION:-}" == "reverted" ]] && _wb_reason="write-boundary-reverted"
604	                    emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" \
605	                        "kind=$kind" "rc=1" "reason=$_wb_reason"
606	                    return 1
607	                fi
608	            fi
609	        fi
610	        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.complete" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
611	    else
612	        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" "rc=$rc"
613	    fi
614	
615	    # #2183: keep THIS attempt's declared outputs before the next dispatch can
616	    # overwrite them. After the rc branches, so a FAILED attempt — the one whose
617	    # record matters most — is archived too. Fail-open by construction.
618	    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && declare -F attempt_archive_outputs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
619	        attempt_archive_outputs "$plugin_dir" "${2:-}" "${1:-}" "$rc" "$_lc_outputs_before" 2>/dev/null || true
620	    fi
621	
622	    # #1823 (ADR-054 §4): the plugin's raw status passes through UNCHANGED, and
623	    # deliberately so during versioned coexistence. A v1 plugin has no result
624	    # field in which to say what its rc says — `plan`'s rc=10 IS its only way to
625	    # report `scope_too_large` — so narrowing here would destroy the meaning of
626	    # every unmigrated plugin at once. The narrowing is gated on the result
627	    # contract at the dispatch boundary instead (see cycle_dispatch_stage), and
628	    # becomes unconditional in #1850 when the last v1 reader is dropped.
629	    return $rc
630	}
